feed.title: NPR Topics: Health
feed.subtitle: Comprehensive health news from NPR. Follow for updates on medical research, wellness trends, public health policy, patient care and healthcare systems.

entry.title: How American Thanksgiving took root -- and evolved -- in Liberia
entry.summary: The first settlers of Liberia were African Americans who brought along the holiday of Thanksgiving — which has evolved to reflect the history and identity of this new nation.

entry.title: This group of seamstresses mends shirts to make chemo easier for cancer patients
entry.summary: Seamstresses in Ohio and other states are making zippered shirts for cancer patients so they can more comfortably undergo chemotherapy treatments.

entry.title: Here's the public health guidance for possible lead exposure in Iowa
entry.summary: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Dr. Dan McCabe, medical director of the Iowa Poison Control Center, about how people can protect themselves after the Army detonates degraded lead azide.

entry.title: Doctors struggle to save babies after parents refuse vitamin K
entry.summary: Doctors are fighting an uphill battle against disinformation about routine vitamin K shots given to newborns in the hospital. It helps prevent a rare but devastating bleeding disorder.

entry.title: The human cost of the electric vehicle boom is at the center of a lawsuit in Congo
entry.summary: A landmark lawsuit in Congo sees 27 residents accuse a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine of poisoning their community and the government of failing to protect them.

entry.title: 'Medicare for all' is back on the drawing board. Does it stand a better chance this time?
entry.summary: Several newly elected Democratic U.S. senators campaigned on Medicare for All. Could this be the time it actually gets traction?

entry.title: Mushroom supplements promise health benefits. What does the science say?
entry.summary: Wellness influencers say mushroom supplements can help with your gut health, focus and immune system. Here is where research suggests there are some links.

entry.title: Meet the young authors! A literacy program inspires kids in South Africa
entry.summary: South Africa is working to overcome a children's literacy crisis. In one Johannesburg township, a reading club is instilling a love of books in kids — and inspiring them to become authors.

entry.title: Medicare looks a bit different in 2027, so don't miss open enrollment
entry.summary: Open enrollment for Medicare runs through Dec. 7, and there are a few different pitfalls people should watch out for this year. Your drug plan or Medicare Advantage plan could be changing a lot.

entry.title: Bayer reaches Roundup settlement that could cost the company billions
entry.summary: The money will go to thousands of people who have been or will be diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma – a blood cancer linked to the herbicide.
